SW-01.title: Flash on the Sun!
SW-01.kidText: A bright flash on the Sun! Fast particles might follow soon.

realScience.text: Flares are graded A, B, C, M, X. Each letter is 10× stronger than the last [S3]. Flare light reaches Earth in ~8 minutes, and fast particles can follow ~20–30 minutes later [S4].

actions.title: Finish the outside job fast
actions.lesson: Racing a storm is a gamble

SW-02.title: Radiation Storm!
SW-02.kidText: Invisible particles from the Sun are here! Hide in the shelter or keep working?

realScience.text: Particles from big solar eruptions arrive within tens of minutes [S4]. In May 2024, Curiosity's radiation detector on Mars recorded its biggest surge since 2012: 8,100 micrograys, like 30 chest X-rays [S6]. Orion crews make a shelter by stacking stowage bags around themselves [S10] within about 30 minutes of an alert [S11]. NASA limits one storm's dose to 250 mSv [S9].

raw.effect: `SH+2` until the storm ends; inside tasks continue

SW-03.title: Storm Cloud Coming
SW-03.kidText: The Sun threw a giant cloud. It reaches Mars in [N] sols! How do we get ready?

realScience.text: A coronal mass ejection (CME) is a huge cloud from the Sun that takes ~1–3 days to reach Earth [S4]. NASA's DONKI models also predict when CMEs reach Mars [S2].

actions.title: Rush science before it hits
actions.lesson: Use the calm before the storm

SW-04.title: The Storm Cloud Hits
SW-04.kidText: The cloud is here! Radios crackle and shields get tested.

realScience.text: In May 2024, at least seven CMEs reached Earth and made the strongest geomagnetic storm in over 20 years [S5]. That same month, Curiosity measured a record radiation jump on Mars [S6].

raw.effect: Can send to Earth / send data

SW-05.title: Quiet Sun Day
SW-05.kidText: The Sun is calm today. A great sol to go outside!

realScience.text: Even on calm days, cosmic rays keep coming. Curiosity measured about 0.64 mSv a day on Mars' surface, about a third of the ~1.8 mSv a day during the flight to Mars [S8].

actions.title: Big science walk
actions.lesson: Calm days are for big trips

SW-06.title: Rays Add Up
SW-06.kidText: Space rays add up a little every sol. Who goes outside next?

realScience.text: Curiosity measured ~0.64 mSv/day on the Martian surface [S8]. NASA's career limit is 600 mSv [S9].

args: Next EVAs go to the lowest-DOSE astronaut (maybe not the expert: −1 SP per EVA)

raw.cost: Next EVAs go to the lowest-DOSE astronaut (maybe not the expert: −1 SP per EVA)

actions.title: Send the expert again

args: Expert's DOSE climbs fastest → SW-07 sooner

actions.lesson: The best person isn't always the safest choice

raw.later: Expert's DOSE climbs fastest → SW-07 sooner

SW-07.title: Dose Badge Turning Red
SW-07.kidText: The crew's radiation badge is almost full!

realScience.text: Artemis crews wear personal radiation badges [S12]. The 600 mSv career limit decides how long an astronaut can fly [S9].

SW-08.title: Earth Is Safe, Mars Is Not
SW-08.kidText: Mission Control says Earth is fine… but the solar cloud is heading for Mars!

realScience.text: NASA's DONKI model runs sometimes report "no or little impact to Earth" while still predicting a CME arrival time at Mars [S2]. Earth and Mars are in different places, so a storm can miss one and hit the other.

actions.title: Trust the Mars forecast, prepare
actions.lesson: Earth's space weather isn't Mars' space weather

raw.effect: Shows the exact storm strength S; `SP+1`

SW-09.title: Forecasters' Message
SW-09.kidText: Real space-weather forecasters sent a message. Read it and decide.

realScience.text: DONKI messages come from NASA's Moon to Mars Space Weather Analysis Office [S2].

args: Answer arrives next sol (`SP+1` for learning)
Too late if a storm comes today

raw.effect: Answer arrives next sol (`SP+1` for learning)
raw.later: Too late if a storm comes today

SW-10.title: Radiation Sensor Glitch
SW-10.kidText: Our radiation sensor stopped. We can't see storms coming!

realScience.text: Orion carries HERA radiation sensors that warn the crew when to take shelter [S12].

actions.title: Use Earth's forecasts

args: Warnings arrive, but one step late (signal delay)
Storms may hit before the warning

actions.lesson: Help from Earth is slow at Mars

raw.later: Storms may hit before the warning

raw.cost: EVA tasks −1 SP each until fixed

PW-01.title: Hot Machine!
PW-01.kidText: The battery box is overheating while it charges! What do we do?

realScience.text: Spacecraft carry heat away with liquid cooling loops and radiators. In 2022 a tiny hole emptied a Soyuz spacecraft's cooling loop [S29].

raw.later: `p=0.4:` ⏳1 loud POP! Max battery 10 → 7 for the rest of the mission (no one hurt)

actions.title: Switch it off to cool
actions.lesson: Turning off is safe but slows you

raw.cost: Battery unusable today (only today's sun power)

PW-02.title: Dusty Solar Panels
PW-02.kidText: Mars dust is covering our solar panels. Less power each sol!

realScience.text: By 2009, dust on rover Spirit's panels let only 25% of sunlight through [S17].

raw.later: If 3 stacks build up → PW-06 (in M2, M5)

PW-03.title: Lucky Wind!
PW-03.kidText: A whirlwind blew the dust off our panels! Extra power today!

realScience.text: In Feb 2009, Martian wind cleaned Spirit's panels: power rose from ~210 to ~240 watt-hours a day. The rover needed ~180 to survive [S17].

PW-04.title: Dust Storm on the Way
PW-04.kidText: Orbiters see a dust storm coming. In 2 sols, sunlight drops a lot.

realScience.text: Normal dust haze ("tau") at Opportunity's site was about 0.5. The rover needed tau below 2 to recharge [S14].

args: Lab off for 2 sols (`LOST: lab SP`)

raw.cost: Lab off for 2 sols (`LOST: lab SP`)

PW-05.title: Planet-Wide Dust Storm
PW-05.kidText: The dust storm covers the whole planet! Day looks like night.

realScience.text: In June 2018 the dust haze reached a record tau of 10.8. Opportunity's power fell 97%, to 21 watt-hours, and the rover never woke up [S15].

actions.title: Keep one experiment running
actions.lesson: Is the science worth the risk?

PW-06.title: Power Fading Slowly
PW-06.kidText: Dust keeps piling up. Every sol there's a bit less power. Which machines stay on?

realScience.text: Dust slowly covered the solar panels of NASA's InSight lander. The team had to run it part-time to save power, and the mission ended in December 2022 [S18].

actions.title: Keep only the most important instrument

args: `LOST: lab SP` except one chosen task type

raw.cost: `LOST: lab SP` except one chosen task type

actions.title: Big cleaning walk (2 people)
actions.lesson: Hard work can reset a slow problem

actions.title: Part-time mode

actions.lesson: Slow and steady can last longer

raw.cost: Lab runs every other sol (half SP)

PW-07.title: Freezing Night
PW-07.kidText: Tonight is super cold! Pipes and batteries hate the cold.

realScience.text: NASA's Viking 1 lander measured Mars air from −89 °C at night to −31 °C by day [S13].

raw.cost: Lab and greenhouse rooms go cold
raw.later: `LOST: lab SP tomorrow`; `p=0.3:` crops 1 sol late

PW-08.title: Not Enough Power!
PW-08.kidText: We need more power than we have. Something must be unplugged!

realScience.text: Mars gets only 43% of the sunlight Earth gets: 586 vs 1,361 watts per square meter [S13].

actions.title: Unplug the lab
actions.lesson: Science waits when power is short

PW-09.title: Cut Cable
PW-09.kidText: A cable to the solar panels got cut. Power is down by half!

realScience.text: In May 2022, NASA's InSight lander felt a magnitude 4.7 marsquake that kept the ground shaking for hours [S49].

PW-10.title: Pick Your Power Plant
PW-10.kidText: How will your Mars base get its power?

realScience.text: NASA's Fission Surface Power reactor aims for 40 kW for 10 years. If it works on the Moon, the design may be updated for Mars [S19]. NASA also sets a separate small dose limit for radiation from nuclear power systems [S9].

args: Cargo space: no extra science kit (science goal +2)

raw.cost: Cargo space: no extra science kit (science goal +2)

LS-01.title: Stuffy Air
LS-01.kidText: The air feels stuffy and people have headaches. CO₂ is building up!

realScience.text: Each astronaut breathes out about 1 kg of CO₂ a day [S21]. On the ISS, headaches start at 2.8–4.5 mmHg of CO₂, so NASA keeps it under 3 mmHg [S22].

actions.title: Fix the CO₂ scrubber
actions.lesson: Fix the cause, not the symptom

LS-02.title: Square Filter, Round Hole
LS-02.kidText: Our spare filters are the wrong shape! Can we build an adapter?

realScience.text: On Apollo 13, the square filters from the command module didn't fit the lunar module's round holder. Mission Control designed an adapter from bags, tape and a flight-plan cover [S23].

actions.title: Ask Mission Control for a plan
actions.lesson: At Mars, help from Earth is slow

raw.effect: The plan arrives next sol → `LS+3` for `ENG.EN-1`

actions.title: Use oxygen tanks to freshen air

LS-03.title: Oxygen Maker Stopped
LS-03.kidText: The machine that makes oxygen from water stopped!

realScience.text: Each person needs about 0.8 kg of oxygen a day [S21]. Backup "oxygen candles" each make enough oxygen for one person for one day [S25].

raw.effect: Air safe for 1 sol; no fire risk

LS-04.title: Smoke!
LS-04.kidText: Smoke alarm! A backup oxygen candle is sparking!

realScience.text: In Feb 1997, an oxygen candle caught fire on the Mir space station [S25]. The crew wore masks, used extinguishers, and no one was hurt [S26].

actions.title: Close that room's hatch
actions.lesson: Isolate a problem to save the rest

raw.cost: Lose that room for 3 sols (lab or greenhouse: the game shows which)

LS-05.title: Water Recycler Clogged
LS-05.kidText: The water recycler is clogged. No clean water from it today!

realScience.text: The ISS recycles water from crew sweat, breath and urine into clean drinking water [S27].

LS-06.title: Upgrade: Brine Processor
LS-06.kidText: We can install a gadget that squeezes more water out of waste!

realScience.text: Adding a Brine Processor raised ISS water recovery from 93–94% to 98% [S27].

LS-07.title: Tiny Leak
LS-07.kidText: Hiss! Air is slowly leaking out of the habitat.

realScience.text: Tiny space rocks or debris can punch small holes. In Dec 2022 one drained the coolant from a Soyuz spacecraft's outer loop [S29].

LS-08.title: Cooling Loop Leak
LS-08.kidText: The cooling liquid is leaking. The base will slowly get too hot inside!

realScience.text: In Dec 2022, a tiny hole let all the coolant leak out of Soyuz MS-22's outer radiator loop in about 18 hours [S29].

LS-09.title: Air or Water?
LS-09.kidText: Our oxygen comes from splitting water. Water is low. Which matters more?

realScience.text: Space stations make oxygen by splitting water (electrolysis) [S28]. Each astronaut also needs at least 2.5 L of drinking water a day [S20].

LS-10.title: Ice Found!
LS-10.kidText: We found ice under the dust! It can become water and even air.

realScience.text: In 2008, NASA's Phoenix lander found and tested ice in the soil of Mars' far north, proving there is water there [S30]. Water can be split into oxygen by electrolysis [S28].

args: Can dig on a later sol
Later digging costs `PWR+1` more (dust covers it)

raw.effect: Can dig on a later sol
raw.later: Later digging costs `PWR+1` more (dust covers it)

LS-11.title: Make Air from Mars Air
LS-11.kidText: Mars air is mostly CO₂. A machine can pull oxygen out of it!

realScience.text: Mars' thin air is about 96% carbon dioxide [S32]. Perseverance's MOXIE made 122 g of oxygen in all, about what a small dog breathes in 10 hours [S31]. At its best it made 12 g per hour [S31b].
Astronauts grew red romaine lettuce from seed to salad in 33 days [S33]. Chile peppers grew for 137 days on the ISS [S34], and radishes were grown there too [S35].

FD-02.title: Flowers Need Help
FD-02.kidText: No bees on Mars! The pepper flowers need help to make peppers.

realScience.text: For the ISS peppers, the team ran fans to spread pollen, and astronauts also pollinated some flowers by hand [S35].

FD-03.title: Old Food Losing Vitamins
FD-03.kidText: Packed food slowly loses vitamins. The crew feels a bit tired.

realScience.text: Food for Mars needs a 5-year shelf life [S36]. Packed space food loses most of its vitamin C after about a year [S37].

FD-04.title: Pack the Cargo
FD-04.kidText: Rockets to Mars can only leave every 26 months. Pick ONE extra crate!

realScience.text: Launch windows to Mars open only about every 26 months [S56], so a Mars crew must live with what it brought.

raw.effect: Unlocks 2 one-time *Kit experiment* tasks (`ME.EN-1` → `SP+2`, no power) (D-013)

FD-05.title: Taco Night!
FD-05.kidText: The peppers are ripe! Have a feast or save them?

realScience.text: In 2021, ISS astronauts made tacos with space-grown chile peppers and sent 12 peppers back to Earth for study [S35].

actions.title: Send samples to scientists
actions.lesson: Your food is also an experiment

raw.effect: `SP+3` (samples wait for the next ship home)

FD-06.title: Food Running Low
FD-06.kidText: Only a few sols of food left!

realScience.text: An astronaut needs about 3,035 kcal a day on average [S20]. On Mars, no delivery can arrive quickly [S56].

raw.later: If food runs low again → MG-02 sooner

FD-07.title: Plants in Mars Soil?
FD-07.kidText: Free soil outside! But is it safe for plants and people?

realScience.text: Mars soil contains about 0.5–1% perchlorate, a salt that's toxic to people because it affects the thyroid [S38].

args: `SP+2`; learn it's unsafe → unlocks a "Wash the soil" task

raw.effect: `SP+2`; learn it's unsafe → unlocks a "Wash the soil" task

CR-01.title: Exercise or Experiment?
CR-01.kidText: Muscles and bones get weaker in low gravity. Exercise or do science?

realScience.text: In weightlessness, astronauts lose about 1–1.5% of their bone density per month, so ISS crews exercise about 2 hours a day [S39]. Mice flown to the ISS lost muscle and bone in 33 days (NASA OSDR data) [S40]. Mars has only 38% of Earth's gravity [S13].

raw.effect: No penalty and no SP lost

CR-02.title: Can't Sleep
CR-02.kidText: [Name] can't sleep. Tomorrow they'll be very tired.

realScience.text: Astronauts sleep an average of about 6 hours a night in space, less than they need [S42].

CR-03.title: Missing Home
CR-03.kidText: [Name] misses their family. A message home would help.

realScience.text: NASA's CHAPEA crew lived 378 days in a pretend Mars habitat [S43], and a message and its reply could take up to 44 minutes [S44].

actions.title: Send a video home
actions.lesson: On Mars you can't call live

raw.effect: `EN+1` now, `+1` more when the reply arrives next sol

CR-04.title: Dust Sneezes
CR-04.kidText: Red dust came inside on the spacesuits. Achoo!

realScience.text: On the Moon, Apollo 17 astronaut Harrison Schmitt got "lunar hay fever" from dust brought inside [S48]. Mars dust adds another problem: the soil contains perchlorate, which is toxic to people [S38].

actions.title: Clean suits in the airlock
actions.lesson: Clean-up is part of the job

actions.title: Ignore it
actions.lesson: Dust inside is a real hazard

CR-05.title: Water in the Helmet!
CR-05.kidText: Water is floating inside [Name]'s helmet! Come back or keep going?

realScience.text: In 2013, water collected in astronaut Luca Parmitano's helmet during a spacewalk. NASA ended the walk early and he got back inside safely [S46]. About 1–1.5 L of water got into his suit [S47].

actions.title: Buddy walks them back
actions.lesson: Teams watch out for each other

raw.effect: Safe, and the suit gets checked (no repeat)

actions.title: Finish the task first
actions.lesson: Never risk a person for a task

CR-06.title: Slip on a Rock
CR-06.kidText: [Name] slipped on a rock outside. Their ankle hurts.

realScience.text: Gravity on Mars is about 38% of Earth's, so walking in a bulky suit feels very different [S13].

actions.title: Tape it and keep going
actions.lesson: Pushing through can make it worse

CR-07.title: Too Tired to Work
CR-07.kidText: The crew is almost out of energy!

realScience.text: Astronauts often sleep less than planned, which makes their work harder [S42].

CR-08.title: Blurry Vision
CR-08.kidText: [Name]'s eyes are a bit blurry. Body fluids shift toward the head in low gravity.

realScience.text: About 70% of long-mission astronauts get eye changes (called SANS) as fluid shifts toward the head [S39].

RS-01.title: Shiny Rock Far Away
RS-01.kidText: Cameras spot an amazing rock, but it's far away!

realScience.text: Spacewalks are usually planned for about 6.5 hours, because suits carry limited air and supplies [S47].

RS-02.title: The Ground Is Shaking!
RS-02.kidText: Rumble! A marsquake is shaking the base.

realScience.text: On 4 May 2022, NASA's InSight felt a magnitude 4.7 marsquake that lasted hours [S49]. InSight detected 1,319 marsquakes in total [S50]. The most active quake area known on Mars is Cerberus Fossae, in Elysium Planitia, where InSight landed [S52].

actions.title: Record it with the seismometer
actions.lesson: Quakes show what's inside a planet

RS-03.title: Lab Machine Broken
RS-03.kidText: The lab's main machine stopped. No experiments until it's fixed!

realScience.text: In January 2016 a CO₂-removal machine on the ISS failed, and two astronauts replaced its broken parts [S55]. Breakdowns happen even on the best stations.

raw.cost: `LOST: half of lab SP until fixed`

RS-04.title: Send Your Data Home
RS-04.kidText: The antenna is ready. Send your science to Earth now?

realScience.text: A signal between Earth and Mars takes about 4 to 20 minutes each way [S54].

RS-05.title: Experiment Results!
RS-05.kidText: Your space-biology experiment is finished. What do we do with it?

realScience.text: In an ISS study, mice lost muscle and bone after 33 days in space, and a treatment helped protect them (the data is in NASA's OSDR) [S40]. NASA's Twins Study found most of Scott Kelly's body changes went back to normal within months of returning [S41].

actions.title: Use it to protect our crew

raw.effect: `SP+1`; CR-01.a costs no SP from now on

RS-06.title: Earth Wants More Science
RS-06.kidText: Mission Control asks: can you do an extra experiment this week?

realScience.text: NASA's CHAPEA crew split their time between simulated Marswalks, robots, habitat repairs, exercise and growing crops [S45].

actions.title: Explain we need repair time
actions.lesson: Speaking up is part of leading

raw.effect: Earth agrees: next "Ask Earth" is free

RS-07.title: Space Rock Hits Mars!
RS-07.kidText: BOOM, far away! A space rock just hit Mars and made a brand-new crater.

realScience.text: InSight felt quakes caused by space rocks hitting Mars. The two biggest impacts made craters about 150 meters wide [S51].

actions.title: Drive out to the fresh crater
actions.lesson: Rare chances can be worth a trip

actions.title: Record the shaking
actions.lesson: Shaking tells where the hit was

CM-01.title: The Sun Is Between Us
CM-01.kidText: Mars is going behind the Sun. No talking to Earth for a while!

realScience.text: About every 2 years, Earth and Mars end up on opposite sides of the Sun. NASA stops sending commands for about 2 weeks and hears nothing at all for about 2 days [S53].

CM-02.title: Antenna Off Target
CM-02.kidText: The antenna isn't pointing at Earth anymore!

realScience.text: Messages between Earth and Mars take about 4 to 20 minutes each way [S54], and only if the antenna points the right way.

CM-03.title: Garbled Message
CM-03.kidText: Mission Control's message came through scrambled!

realScience.text: Big X-class flares can cause radio blackouts [S3].

actions.title: Guess what they meant
actions.lesson: Guessing saves time but risks mistakes

actions.title: Use our own judgment
actions.lesson: Far-away crews must think for themselves

MG-01.title: Choose Your Base
MG-01.kidText: Where on Mars will you build your base?

realScience.text: Curiosity measured surface radiation at Gale crater [S7]. Perseverance, which carried MOXIE, explores Jezero crater [S60][S31]. Phoenix found ice, and also perchlorate, in the far northern plains [S30][S38].

MG-02.title: Go Home Early?
MG-02.kidText: Things are going badly. Keep going, or end the mission safely?

realScience.text: When Apollo 13 lost power and oxygen, the crew gave up the Moon landing and focused on getting home safely [S24].

actions.lesson: Knowing when to stop is brave

MG-03.title: Crew Disagreement
MG-03.kidText: The Engineer wants to fix the panels. The Researcher wants to explore. There's only power for one!

realScience.text: NASA's CHAPEA crew had to handle limited resources, isolation and slow messages to Earth [S44].

MG-04.title: The Long Trip
MG-04.kidText: Before you land, you fly for months through deep space. How will you travel?

realScience.text: During the flight to Mars, Curiosity's detector measured about 1.8 mSv a day. A round trip alone would give about 0.66 Sv, more than NASA's 600 mSv career limit [S8][S9].

stories.title: Radiation Storm!
stories.happens: Invisible bits from the Sun are here! They can fill up your radiation badges.
stories.trueStory: In May 2024, the Curiosity rover on Mars measured its biggest radiation jump in 12 years. That's like getting 30 X-rays!

stories.title: Storm Cloud Coming
stories.happens: The Sun threw a giant cloud into space. It reaches Mars in a few sols!
stories.trueStory: NASA computers can predict when these clouds will reach Mars.

stories.title: The Storm Cloud Hits
stories.happens: The cloud is here! Radios crackle and the shields get tested.
stories.trueStory: In May 2024, many of these clouds hit Earth and made the biggest space storm in 20 years.

stories.title: Quiet Sun Day
stories.happens: The Sun is calm. A great day to go outside!
stories.trueStory: Even on calm days, tiny space rays keep coming. On Mars you get about a third of what you'd get flying through space.

stories.title: Rays Add Up
stories.happens: Radiation badges fill up a little every sol. Who goes outside next?
stories.trueStory: NASA has a lifetime limit for how much radiation an astronaut can get.

stories.title: Badge Turning Red
stories.happens: The crew's radiation badge is almost full!
stories.trueStory: Real astronauts wear radiation badges, just like in the game.

stories.title: Earth Is Safe, Mars Is Not
stories.happens: Earth says "no problem"… but the Sun's cloud is heading for Mars!
stories.trueStory: Sometimes NASA's model says a cloud will miss Earth but hit Mars. Earth and Mars are in different places!

stories.title: Message from Space-Weather Forecasters
stories.happens: Real forecasters sent a message about the Sun.
stories.trueStory: NASA has a real team that watches the Sun for trips to the Moon and Mars.

stories.title: Radiation Sensor Broken
stories.happens: You can't see storms coming!
stories.trueStory: NASA's Orion spaceship has radiation sensors that tell astronauts when to hide.

stories.title: Hot Machine!
stories.happens: The battery box is getting too hot!
stories.trueStory: Spaceships use cooling pipes full of liquid to carry heat away.

stories.title: Dusty Solar Panels
stories.happens: Dust covers the solar panels. Less power every sol!
stories.trueStory: The Spirit rover's panels got so dusty that only a quarter of the sunlight got through.

stories.title: Lucky Wind!
stories.happens: A whirlwind blew the dust off your panels. Extra power!
stories.trueStory: In 2009, a Martian wind cleaned the Spirit rover's panels and gave it more power.

stories.title: Dust Storm Coming
stories.happens: Satellites see a dust storm. Soon the Sun will be hard to see.
stories.trueStory: The Opportunity rover needed a fairly clear sky to recharge its batteries.

stories.title: Planet-Wide Dust Storm
stories.happens: Dust covers ALL of Mars. Day looks like night!
stories.trueStory: In 2018, a giant dust storm cut Opportunity's power by 97%. It never woke up again.

stories.title: Power Fading Slowly
stories.happens: Dust keeps piling up, and there's a little less power each sol.
stories.trueStory: Dust slowly covered the InSight lander's solar panels, and its mission ended in 2022.

stories.title: Freezing Night
stories.happens: Tonight is super cold!
stories.trueStory: A NASA lander measured −89 °C on a Mars night!

stories.title: Not Enough Power!
stories.happens: You need more power than you have. Something must be unplugged!
stories.trueStory: Mars gets less than half the sunlight Earth gets.

stories.title: Cut Cable
stories.happens: A power cable got cut. Half your power is gone!
stories.trueStory: The biggest marsquake ever measured shook the ground for hours.

stories.title: Pick Your Power Plant
stories.happens: How will your base get its power?
stories.trueStory: NASA is designing a small reactor that could power a base for 10 years.

stories.title: Stuffy Air
stories.happens: The air feels stuffy and people get headaches. Too much breathed-out air (CO₂)!
stories.trueStory: Each astronaut breathes out about 1 kg of CO₂ every day!

stories.title: Square Filter, Round Hole
stories.happens: The spare filters are the wrong shape!
stories.trueStory: On Apollo 13, astronauts built an adapter from bags, tape and a book cover, and it saved them!

stories.title: Oxygen Maker Stopped
stories.happens: The machine that makes air from water stopped!
stories.trueStory: Each person needs about 0.8 kg of oxygen every day.

stories.title: Smoke!
stories.happens: The smoke alarm is beeping! The oxygen candle is sparking.
stories.trueStory: In 1997, an oxygen candle caught fire on the Mir space station. The crew put it out and everyone was OK.

stories.title: Water Recycler Clogged
stories.happens: The machine that cleans water is clogged!
stories.trueStory: The space station turns sweat, breath and even pee back into clean drinking water!

stories.title: Water-Saving Gadget
stories.happens: You can install a gadget that saves even more water.
stories.trueStory: A new gadget helped the space station recycle 98% of its water.

stories.title: Tiny Leak
stories.happens: Hissss! Air is slowly leaking out.
stories.trueStory: Tiny space rocks can punch little holes in spaceships.

stories.title: Cooling Leak
stories.happens: The cooling liquid is leaking. The base will slowly get too hot inside!
stories.trueStory: In 2022, a tiny hole let all the cooling liquid leak out of a Soyuz spaceship in about 18 hours.

stories.title: Air or Water?
stories.happens: You make air by splitting water, but water is running low!
stories.trueStory: Space stations really do make their oxygen by splitting water.

stories.title: Ice Found!
stories.happens: There's ice under the dust! It can become water, and even air.
stories.trueStory: In 2008, NASA's Phoenix lander found ice on Mars!

stories.title: Make Air from Mars Air
stories.happens: Mars air is mostly CO₂. A machine can pull oxygen out of it!
stories.trueStory: The MOXIE machine on Mars made oxygen. In total, about what a small dog breathes in 10 hours!

stories.title: What Should We Plant?
stories.happens: Pick seeds for your greenhouse!
stories.trueStory: Astronauts grew lettuce in space, from seed to salad in 33 days!

stories.title: Flowers Need Help
stories.happens: There are no bees on Mars! Pepper flowers need help to make peppers.
stories.trueStory: Astronauts helped space peppers by hand and with fans.

stories.title: Old Food Losing Vitamins
stories.happens: Packed food slowly loses its vitamins. The crew feels tired.
stories.trueStory: After about a year, packed space food has lost most of its vitamin C.

stories.title: Pack the Cargo
stories.happens: Before you go, pick ONE extra crate!
stories.trueStory: Rockets can only leave for Mars about every 26 months, so you live with what you bring!

stories.title: Taco Night!
stories.happens: The peppers are ripe!
stories.trueStory: In 2021, astronauts made tacos with peppers they grew in space!

stories.title: Food Running Low
stories.happens: Only a few days of food left!
stories.trueStory: An astronaut needs about 3,000 calories a day.

stories.title: Plants in Mars Soil?
stories.happens: There's free soil outside, but is it safe?
stories.trueStory: Mars soil has a salt called perchlorate that's bad for people.

stories.title: Exercise or Experiment?
stories.happens: Muscles and bones get weaker in low gravity.
stories.trueStory: On the space station, astronauts exercise about 2 hours every day to keep their bones strong.

stories.title: Can't Sleep
stories.happens: An astronaut can't fall asleep.
stories.trueStory: Astronauts sleep only about 6 hours a night in space. That is less than they need!

stories.title: Missing Home
stories.happens: An astronaut misses their family.
stories.trueStory: NASA's practice Mars crew waited up to 44 minutes for an answer from Earth.

stories.title: Dust Sneezes
stories.happens: Dust came inside on the spacesuits. Achoo!
stories.trueStory: On the Moon, astronaut Harrison Schmitt got "Moon hay fever" from dust!

stories.title: Water in the Helmet!
stories.happens: Water is floating inside an astronaut's helmet during a spacewalk!
stories.trueStory: In 2013, this really happened to astronaut Luca Parmitano. NASA brought him back inside safely.

stories.title: Slip on a Rock
stories.happens: An astronaut slipped outside and hurt their ankle.
stories.trueStory: Mars gravity is only about a third of Earth's, so walking feels very different.

stories.title: Too Tired to Work
stories.happens: The crew is almost out of energy!
stories.trueStory: Tired astronauts find their work harder, just like tired kids!

stories.title: Blurry Vision
stories.happens: An astronaut's eyes are a bit blurry.
stories.trueStory: In low gravity, body fluids float up toward the head, and that can change astronauts' eyes.

stories.title: Shiny Rock Far Away
stories.happens: Cameras see an amazing rock… but it's far away!
stories.trueStory: Spacewalks usually last about 6 and a half hours, because suits only carry so much air.

stories.title: Marsquake!
stories.happens: Rumble! The ground is shaking.
stories.trueStory: NASA's InSight lander felt 1,319 marsquakes!

stories.title: Lab Machine Broken
stories.happens: The lab's main machine stopped working.
stories.trueStory: Machines on the space station break sometimes, and astronauts fix them.

stories.title: Send Your Data Home
stories.happens: The antenna is ready! Your science stars only count once they reach Earth.
stories.trueStory: A message from Mars takes 4 to 20 minutes to reach Earth.

stories.title: Experiment Results!
stories.happens: Your space experiment is finished!
stories.trueStory: Mice that flew to the space station lost muscle and bone in 33 days. Scientists study this to protect astronauts.

stories.title: Earth Wants More Science
stories.happens: Mission Control asks for an extra experiment.
stories.trueStory: NASA's practice Mars crew had to juggle science, repairs, exercise and gardening.

stories.title: Space Rock Hits Mars!
stories.happens: BOOM, far away! A space rock made a brand-new crater.
stories.trueStory: InSight felt space rocks hit Mars. The biggest ones made craters about 150 meters across, wider than a football field is long!

stories.title: The Sun Is Between Us
stories.happens: Mars is going behind the Sun. No talking to Earth for a while!
stories.trueStory: About every 2 years, NASA stops sending commands to Mars for about 2 weeks because the Sun is in the way.

stories.title: Antenna Off Target
stories.happens: The antenna isn't pointing at Earth anymore!
stories.trueStory: Messages only reach Earth if the antenna points the right way.

stories.title: Garbled Message
stories.happens: Mission Control's message came through scrambled!
stories.trueStory: Big X-class flares can scramble radio signals.

stories.title: Choose Your Base
stories.happens: Where will you build?
stories.trueStory: Real NASA rovers and landers have explored all three places!

stories.title: Go Home Early?
stories.happens: Things are going badly. Keep going or go home safely?
stories.trueStory: When Apollo 13 had a big problem, the crew skipped the Moon landing and got home safely. That was brave!

stories.title: Crew Disagreement
stories.happens: The Engineer wants to fix the panels. The Researcher wants to explore. There's only power for one!
stories.trueStory: NASA's practice Mars crew had to share limited supplies and work it out together.

stories.title: The Long Trip
stories.happens: Before landing, you fly through space for months. How will you travel?
stories.trueStory: The trip to Mars gives more radiation than living on Mars does!
